summary: This is Snowflake's reference page for the ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW command, which changes an existing materialized view in the current or specified schema. It lists supported actions (rename, suspend/resume maintenance, cluster, drop clustering key, suspend/resume reclustering, set/unset secure and comment) with the syntax, parameter explanations, usage notes and examples. The page notes that materialized views require Enterprise Edition and that renaming a view does not update dependent views.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW command, covering renaming, suspending/resuming, clustering and secure/comment settings.
key_facts: Materialized views require Snowflake Enterprise Edition.
ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW alters a materialized view in the current or specified schema.
RENAME TO new_name can also move the object to a different database and/or schema using a qualified new name.
The destination database and/or schema must already exist, and an object with the same name cannot already exist in the new location.
Moving an object to a managed access schema is prohibited unless the object owner also owns the target schema.
Renaming a materialized view does not update references to it; a view V1 built on it becomes out of date.
CLUSTER BY (expr) clusters the materialized view to improve performance for queries filtering on the clustering key expressions.
SUSPEND suspends maintenance and use of the materialized view; updates to the base table are not propagated while suspended.
Suspending a clustered materialized view implicitly suspends its reclustering.
RESUME resumes use and maintenance of the view and, if clustered, implicitly resumes reclustering.
SET SECURE turns the view into a secure view, and SET COMMENT = 'string' sets a comment with no effect on behavior.
UNSET supports SECURE, TAG tag_name [, tag_name ...], and COMMENT.
Example: ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW table1_MV RENAME TO my_mv;
Example: ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW my_mv SUSPEND RECLUSTER; suspends clustering but not use of the view.
